newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil firms raise pump prices further.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil firms raise pump prices further.

text.p: Major oil firms in Thailand have raised their pump prices this week for the third time following the de facto devaluation of the baht earlier this month, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand on Wednesday again increased its retail prices, which are viewed as benchmarks in the local market, by 15 satangs per litre.
After the adjustment, PTT unleaded gasoline stood at 9.88 baht ($0.29) per litre and diesel oil at 8.75 baht per litre.

The move came after other major oil firms adjusted their prices, also for the third time. Most foreign firms raised their pump prices by 15 satangs per litre on Saturday and Bangchak Petroleum Plc raised its prices on Wednesday.
A PTT official said the hike reflected the higher cost incurred by the weaker baht.
The baht lost about 20 percent of its value after the government changed to a managed float system from a 13-year old regime of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies.
